audit.why: 46.15% over 26 games and a chart that gives Tahm Kench 4/7 stages. The page already frames this as a lane Akshan does not win by force, only through the level-6-to-Youmuu's window. Kept, matching the mirror at audits/top/tahmkench__akshan.json.

Lvl 1-2 chip, Lvl 6 Comeuppance, Youmuu's, and Tahm's Lvl 3+ threat window are correctly placed; the mirror puts Akshan's only genuine edge at 6 for the same reason. Only the ability slots inside the spikes were wrong.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tahm Kench's slots are scrambled throughout. The page credits Devour to W ('devours you with W', 'his second W charge') when Devour is R; it credits the grey-health self-heal to W when that is Thick Skin (E); and it invents 'W lashes' that stack a slow. It also presents Tongue Lash as an unconditional stun.
audit.why: Riot's text: Tongue Lash (Q) damages, slows and heals him, and applies a stack of An Acquired Taste — 'If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed.' Thick Skin (E) is the grey-health store and the shield conversion, on a 3s cooldown. W is Abyssal Dive, a knockup relocation. R is Devour. The stun is conditional on stack count, which is the whole timing game of the lane — and the page told the reader to fear a stun that is only live one Q in three.
audit.corrected: Tongue Lash (Q, 900 range, 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s) slows and heals; it stuns only on the third An Acquired Taste stack, which consumes them. Thick Skin (E) banks damage as grey health and converts it to a shield every 3s. Devour is R. Three stacks buy either the stun or Devour, never both.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither of the two decisive mechanical interactions appears: Heroic Swing ends on champion collision, and Comeuppance stops on the first body in line.
audit.why: Riot's text for Heroic Swing: he 'gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain.' A 6000-HP Tahm Kench simply standing in the arc ends the swing — he does not need to bait the anchor. Riot's text for Comeuppance: damage 'to the first champion, minion, or structure hit', so a single caster minion eats the whole ultimate. Both are reused from the mirror audit, which reached the same two conclusions from the same source.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'When his Q tongue is on cooldown' with no number, in the one matchup where the commit window IS the cooldown.
audit.why: Tongue Lash is 7s at rank 1 down to 5s at rank 5. Combined with the three-stack rule that is the entire timing model of this lane.

edits.before: Land the long-range Q tongue to stun you, then stack W lashes for the slow and walk you down
edits.after: Build three An Acquired Taste stacks so Tongue Lash (Q) stuns, then walk you down on the slow

edits.before: Soak your Q and passive poke into grey health and let his W heal / percent-HP passive erase every trade
edits.after: Soak your Q and passive poke into Thick Skin (E) grey health and hand it back as a shield every 3s

edits.before: Catch you committed mid-E (Heroic Swing) or out of position and devour you with W toward his turret or jungler
edits.after: Stand in your Heroic Swing arc to knock you off it, then Devour (R) you toward his turret or his jungler

edits.before: Your lethality spike lets E-Q-passive-R actually threaten, but you must commit it when his Q tongue is on cooldown — eat the stun and he devours you (W) under his turret or toward his jungler.
edits.after: Your lethality spike lets E-Q-passive-R actually threaten, but commit only while Tongue Lash (Q) sits on its 7s cooldown — eat the third-stack stun and Devour (R) drags you under his turret.

edits.before: His threat window — Tahm lands a long-range Q tongue to stun you, stacks his W lashes for the slow, and either kills you outright or swallows you with his second W charge.
edits.after: His threat window — three An Acquired Taste stacks turn Tongue Lash (Q) into a stun, and he spends those stacks on the stun or on Devour (R), never both. Count them before you swing.

edits.before: Tahm Kench's early game is built on that long-range Q tongue: it stuns you, and his W lashes stack a slow that lets him walk you down or swallow you whole. Don't step to autorange to land a Q on him where his tongue out-ranges your trade; throw Avengerang from max range on the out-and-back arc and only weave your passive second shot when his Q is on cooldown. The trap is that your chip half-vanishes into his grey health and his W self-heal and percent-HP passive recover the rest, so a 'winning' poke trade nets you nothing while one tongue stun nets him a kill.
edits.after: Tahm Kench's early game is built on Tongue Lash (Q, 900 range, 7s): it slows, heals him, and stacks An Acquired Taste — and only the THIRD stack stuns, so count them and you know exactly when the stun is live. Throw Avengerang from max range on the out-and-back arc and weave your passive second shot while his Q is down. The trap is that your chip half-vanishes into Thick Skin (E) grey health, which he converts back into a shield every 3s, so a 'winning' poke trade nets you nothing while one stun nets him a kill.

edits.before: Your passive second shot stacks toward the third-hit bonus, but every point of Q poke half-converts to grey health his W and percent passive recover — the trade nets out roughly even.
edits.after: Your passive second shot stacks toward the third-hit bonus, but Q poke half-converts to grey health that Thick Skin (E) returns as a shield every 3s — the trade nets out roughly even.

edits.before: Heroic Swing (E) gives you a wall-swing poke-and-escape, yet his Q tongue stun still threatens to catch you mid-swing into a devour — it stays a coinflip on his tongue cooldown.
edits.after: Heroic Swing (E) is a wall-swing poke-and-escape, but he ends it by standing in the arc — champion collision knocks you off — and a third-stack stun turns that into a Devour.

edits.before: Tahm's W lashes slow plus the devour threat let him win the sustained brawl your chip damage can't close against grey health and his self-heal.
edits.after: Tongue Lash slows and heals him every 6s while Thick Skin banks the rest — he wins any sustained brawl your chip damage cannot close before the stun lands.

edits.before: Long game is his. Once Tahm has two items he's a grey-health drain-tank your lethality can't punch through — your double-shot and R just feed his W heal and passive — and his R lets him roam across the map to turn lane pressure into picks, which your W (mostly a lane roam/reset tool here) can't trade evenly. You have to convert the level-6-to-Youmuu's window into a real lead or a turret plate, then use R to pick off-lane. If the game stretches past your lethality spike, he simply out-sustains and out-utilities you.
edits.after: Long game is his. Two items in, Thick Skin (E) banks your whole poke pattern and hands it back as a shield every 3s, and Devour (R) ferries an ally across the map to turn lane pressure into picks. Worse, Comeuppance stops on the first champion, minion or structure in line, so he only has to keep a caster between you to eat the entire ultimate. Convert the level-6-to-Youmuu's window into a real lead or a turret plate, then pick off-lane with R before he out-sustains and out-utilities you.

notes: Every reference to Tahm Kench's W on this page was wrong: Devour is R, the grey health is Thick Skin (E), and 'W lashes' do not exist (W is Abyssal Dive, a knockup). The bigger fix is the stun — Tongue Lash only stuns on the third An Acquired Taste stack and consumes them, so the reader can count stacks instead of fearing every Q. Reused the two decisive interactions the mirror at audits/top/tahmkench__akshan.json had already established (champion collision ends Heroic Swing; the first body in line eats Comeuppance) and stated them from Akshan's side. I deliberately did not repeat the mirror's '120s Devour' figure because the kit file lists Devour's cooldown as 0 and I could not confirm the number locally.
